requestedActions.title: Read issue titles in accessible projects, including pagination

guide.summary: OAuth is documented for third-party apps. Register a user-owned OAuth app in a representative test account, authorize with the read_api scope, and call the project issues endpoint with a Bearer OAuth token. read_api is read-only but broader than issues: it grants read access to all groups and projects the user can access, and no issue-only scope is documented. Pagination continuation is only partly documented. Customer admin and provider review requirements remain unknown.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read issue titles in accessible projects, including pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.
guide.nextAction: Register a test OAuth app in the representative account

findings.title: read_api covers read access to project issues
findings.detail: read_api grants read access to the API, including projects, and the project issues endpoint is documented as a GET call. Request read_api only. It is documented as read-only, but it is broader than issue titles.

evidence.quote: read_api Grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, and the package registry.

findings.title: Real token boundary is broader than issues
findings.detail: The narrowest documented scope for this read is read_api. It covers all groups and projects the authorized user can access, and no issue-only scope is documented. Do not describe the token as limited to issue titles.

evidence.quote: read_api Grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, and the package registry.
Scope Description api Grants complete read/write access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, the dependency proxy, and the package registry.

findings.title: Use the OAuth Bearer header, not a personal token header
findings.detail: The token may go in the Authorization header or as a GET parameter, but not both. Personal access token examples use PRIVATE-TOKEN and must not be copied for OAuth calls.

evidence.quote: You can pass the token either as a GET parameter or in the Authorization header, but not both.
--header "Authorization: Bearer <OAUTH-TOKEN>" \
The preferred way to do this is by using personal access tokens .

findings.title: Each connected person approves access for their own account
findings.detail: The authorization page asks the signed-in user to approve the app's request to access their account. Each individual customer connects their own account. Whether a customer administrator must approve is not documented in the supplied sources.
findings.appliesWhen: Individual customer accounts connect through OAuth.
